HbA1c Test: Purpose, Procedure, Normal Range & Results
May 26, 2026 - By Lupin Diagnostics
India has over 10.1 crore people living with diabetes. A daily finger-prick reading captures just one moment. The HbA1c test normal range tells a fuller story. This simple blood test reveals your average blood sugar over three months. Here is everything you need to know about it.
What Is the HbA1c Test and How Does It Work?
Glucose in your blood naturally sticks to haemoglobin, the protein inside red blood cells. The more sugar in your blood, the more gets attached. Since red blood cells live for roughly three months, the HbA1c test captures your average blood sugar level over that entire period.
This makes it far more reliable than a single fasting reading. A fasting test changes with your last meal or stress levels. Glycated haemoglobin, on the other hand, reflects steady patterns. Think of it as a three-month report card for your blood sugar.
Here is how it differs from routine glucose checks:
A fasting blood sugar test measures glucose at one point in time.
The HbA1c test shows a percentage reflecting 90-day glucose control.
It does not swing based on a recent meal or exercise session.


For more information kindly click on the below link.

When a blood sample is left to stand in a thin glass tube, the red blood cells gradually sink to the bottom. The speed at which they settle is called the 'erythrocyte sedimentation rate' (ESR). In healthy blood, this happens slowly. When inflammation is present, the cells tend to clump together and sink more quickly than usual. ESR is a simple, widely used marker for inflammation. This article breaks down the ESR normal range, what high readings mean, and when to seek further evaluation.

But here's something many people don't realise: the way cholesterol affects men and women can differ significantly. This article breaks down those differences and what you can do about them.

How much do you really know about your kidneys? These two small organs perform some of the most important functions for the body, such as filtering waste and maintaining healthy blood pressure. Globally, about 674 million people have chronic kidney disease. A kidney function test (KFT) is very important for detecting kidney problems early, before they get worse. If you know how to read this test, you can take steps to keep your kidneys healthy.

For more information, please click on the link below.

Your liver handles a lot: filtering toxins, making proteins, and producing digestive enzymes. Since your liver works silently, most damage often goes unnoticed until it becomes serious. An LFT is a group of blood tests that check how well the liver is performing.

The test typically measures ALT (SGPT), AST (SGOT), bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, and albumin levels. Together, these markers reveal the type and location of liver damage. Unlike a single blood sugar reading, an LFT panel paints a broader picture of your liver's overall health.

Early detection matters! The WHO states that 254 million people were diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B in 2022, with an increase of 1.2 million every year. In 2022 alone, the infection caused roughly 1.1 million deaths, mostly from cirrhosis and liver cancer.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently had a CT scan, and I must say it was a surprisingly smooth experience. The staff at the facility were incredibly professional and made me feel at ease right from the start. They explained the entire process clearly, which helped alleviate any anxiety I had.

Overall, I would highly recommend getting a CT scan if needed. It’s a valuable diagnostic tool, and with the right facility, it can be a comfortable and reassuring experience.
